html:
The siege of Sarajevo lasted from April 1992 to February 1996, when Bosnian Serb forces surrounded the capital of Bosnia and Herzegovina and shelled it from the hills, the longest siege of a capital city in modern warfare.

About 11,000 people were killed, among them more than a thousand children. Snipers made crossing streets deadly, and residents lived without regular water, power or heat. The main supply line was a tunnel dug under the airport in 1993. Shells that hit the Markale market in 1994 and 1995 killed dozens and pushed NATO toward air strikes. The National Library burned with much of its collection in 1992. The siege ended after the Dayton Agreement, part of the Bosnian War.
sum: The siege of Sarajevo lasted from April 1992 to February 1996, when Bosnian Serb forces surrounded the capital of Bosnia and Herzegovina and shelled it from the hills, the longest siege of a capital city in modern warfare.
